_about: Earth landform families on the mood board: mechanism, driving variables, timescale, colour source, and how our controls (Recipe C/Si/O, Sea, Heat, Light, Time, Hunger) push a world toward or away from each. Mechanism fields are Earth geology; control_response fields are [game] extrapolation unless prefixed [sci]. Evidence tags/status per research/silicon-life/README.md. Notes: research/world-forms/notes/01-earth-landforms.md. Compiled 2026-11-07.

landforms.name: Natural arch / bridge
landforms.mechanism: Thick porous sandstone over a salt layer -> salt flows and domes the rock -> parallel joints crack it into thin fins -> water, frost and grain-loss eat the fin sides -> a hole breaks through -> stress concentrates in the remaining span; loaded grains are locked and resist erosion while unloaded grains fall, so the form self-shapes toward a stable arch (negative feedback) -> eventually the span thins and collapses.
landforms.timescale: Fins over 10^5-10^6 yr; individual arches persist ~10^4-10^5 yr [INFERRED]; collapses are observed in human lifetimes (Wall Arch, 2008).
colour_sources: bleached zones where reducing fluids removed iron (white/cream)

control_response.recipe: Si+O toward: quartz sandstone is the arch-maker. [game] Builder-made arches (R12) are a second, life-built route.
control_response.sea: Water toward (seepage + frost). Acid toward but faster/rougher (dissolves cement). Methane away (no dissolution, cold-locked).
control_response.heat: Cool-to-mild with freeze-thaw crossings toward; very cold (always frozen) or very hot-dry slows it.
control_response.time: Strong: needs mid-old worlds; very old worlds show collapsed arches and lone pillars.

landforms.name: Hoodoo / spire
landforms.mechanism: Flat-lying layers of weak, carbonate-cemented rock with harder bands -> plateau edge cracked by joints into fins -> frost wedging widens cracks (water expands ~9% on freezing) -> fins perforate into windows, windows collapse into free-standing columns -> slightly acidic rain dissolves the CaCO3 cement, rounding the soft bands and leaving a lumpy, 'totem' profile under a harder cap.
drivers: carbonate dissolution by weakly acidic rain
landforms.timescale: Bryce sees >170 freeze-thaw nights per year (NPS); rim retreat of order 1 ft (~0.3 m) per few decades is often quoted [POP]; a hoodoo field lives ~10^4-10^5 yr.

examples.name: Bryce Amphitheater
examples.place: Bryce Canyon National Park, Utah, USA (Claron Formation)

control_response.recipe: C+O toward on Earth (carbonate cement). Si+O toward if layers have hard/soft contrast.
control_response.sea: Water strongly toward (freeze-thaw). Acid toward (dissolution). Methane/ammonia: only if surface temperature crosses that solvent's freezing point [INFERRED].
control_response.heat: Peaks where daily temperature straddles the sea's freezing point; away at both extremes.
control_response.time: Mid-old; very old flattens to badland/plain.

landforms.name: Fairy chimney (capped tuff cone)
landforms.mechanism: Volcanic ash falls and welds into thick soft tuff (ignimbrite), topped by a harder lava/welded layer -> rain and runoff cut gullies -> harder cap blocks shield the tuff beneath -> cones/pillars with a 'hat' remain -> cap falls, the cone erodes away fast.
landforms.timescale: Tuff laid down over ~10^6-10^7 yr (Miocene-Pliocene); chimneys sculpted over ~10^4-10^5 yr; uncapped cones decay in centuries-millennia [INFERRED].

control_response.recipe: Si+O toward (silicate ash). [game] Heat + Si = volcanic ash plains.
control_response.sea: Water toward (rain). Others neutral.
control_response.heat: Hot (volcanism makes the ash) then mild (rain sculpts).
control_response.time: Mid: young = ash plain, mid = chimneys, old = bare.

landforms.name: Honeycomb / tafoni / alveolar weathering
landforms.mechanism: Salty moisture (sea spray, groundwater) wicks into porous rock -> water evaporates in a slight hollow, salt crystallises in pores and pries grains loose -> hollow deepens; wind across the hollow speeds evaporation inside it and shelters the rims (which also get a protective case-hardened crust) -> positive feedback grows cells of similar size, 'cells within cells'.
landforms.timescale: Visible pitting in decades on coastal sandstone (seawalls); large tafoni over centuries-millennia.

examples.name: Tafoni at Bean Hollow State Beach

control_response.recipe: Si+O toward (porous sandstone/granite). O toward (iron-crusted rims).
control_response.sea: Water and acid toward (dissolved salts); salty coasts strongest. Methane away (no dissolved ions to crystallise) [INFERRED].
control_response.heat: Warm, alternately wet and dry toward.
control_response.hunger: Neutral abiotically; [game] R12 makes inhabited pores glow.

landforms.status: plausible/theorised (salt + wind best supported; exact mix debated)

landforms.name: Bio-pitted rock (phytokarst / bioerosion sponge texture)
landforms.mechanism: Microbes (cyanobacteria, algae, fungi) bore into and dissolve carbonate rock surfaces -> grazers (snails, chitons, urchins) rasp the colonised surface to eat them -> the rock becomes a jagged, black, sponge-like field of pits and spikes; parrotfish grinding coral turns reef into sand.
landforms.timescale: mm-per-year-scale surface lowering on tropical carbonate coasts; spongy fields over centuries-millennia.
colour_sources: black/grey endolithic microbes and their pigments
white fresh carbonate in the pits

control_response.recipe: C+O rock toward on Earth; [game] any soluble stone toward.
control_response.sea: Water, acid toward.
control_response.light: Bright toward: photosynthetic borers need it. [sci]
control_response.hunger: Strong toward: more grazers = more pitting and sand. [sci] analogue; [game] scaling.

landforms.name: Slot canyon
landforms.mechanism: Massive, uniform sandstone with a joint -> rare desert flash floods funnel along the joint carrying sand and gravel -> abrasion and plucking cut down faster than the walls retreat (dry climate, few side tributaries) -> deep, narrow, wave-sculpted corridor.
landforms.timescale: Incision of order 10^4-10^6 yr; walls re-polished every flood.

examples.name: Lower Antelope Canyon
examples.place: Navajo Nation, near Page, Arizona, USA (Navajo Sandstone)

control_response.recipe: Si+O toward (quartz sandstone).
control_response.sea: Water toward; acid toward (faster). Methane: Titan has rain-cut channels too [INFERRED, see notes/02].
control_response.light: Neutral (but shafts of light make it photogenic).

landforms.name: Mesa / butte / monolith
landforms.mechanism: Flat-lying strata with a resistant caprock over soft rock -> uplift lets rivers cut down -> cliffs retreat sideways as soft rock under the cap is undercut and the cap breaks off -> plateau splits into mesas (wider than tall) -> buttes (taller than wide) -> spires -> nothing.

control_response.recipe: Si+O toward (layered sediment); O toward red.
control_response.sea: Water toward (rivers). [game] any flowing sea works.
control_response.heat: Hot-arid toward (steep cliffs survive; humid climates soften slopes).
control_response.time: Strong: the mesa->butte->spire sequence IS the clock. Good Time readout.

landforms.name: Sea cave -> sea arch -> sea stack -> stump
landforms.mechanism: Waves attack a headland -> hydraulic pressure and thrown-sand abrasion exploit joints/faults -> caves form on both sides -> caves meet as an arch -> arch roof collapses -> stack stands alone -> stack is undercut to a stump.
landforms.timescale: Soft limestone/chalk coasts retreat cm/yr; arch-to-stack collapses observed (London Arch, Victoria, 1990; a Twelve Apostles stack, 2005).

examples.name: Twelve Apostles
examples.place: Port Campbell National Park, Victoria, Australia

control_response.recipe: Any rock; carbonate (C+O) and chalk fastest.
control_response.sea: Any liquid sea with waves toward; dense acid/water seas strongest. [INFERRED] Titan's seas are calm (low wave heights) so methane weakens it.
control_response.time: Young = cliffs, mid = arches, old = stacks and stumps.
control_response.hunger: Weak: bioeroders at the waterline speed undercutting [sci].

landforms.name: Travertine terraces (rimstone pools)
landforms.mechanism: CO2-rich groundwater dissolves limestone at depth -> emerges at a spring -> CO2 degasses as it flows, pushing CaCO3 past saturation -> calcite precipitates fastest where water is thin and fast (pool rims) -> rims grow up into dams, pools fill behind them -> staircase of terraces (self-organising positive feedback).
landforms.timescale: mm to cm per year at active vents; terraces reshape in months-years, whole edifices in 10^2-10^4 yr.
colour_sources: microbial mats in warm channels (orange, brown, green)

control_response.recipe: C+O toward (carbonate). [game] Si+O gives the silica version (sinter terraces).
control_response.sea: Water toward (carbonate system). Acid away (keeps carbonate dissolved).
control_response.hunger: Neutral; mats are producers, not hunters.

landforms.name: Silica sinter (geyserite) mounds and terraces
landforms.mechanism: Hot water dissolves silica from deep volcanic rock (silica solubility rises with temperature) -> water reaches the surface, cools and evaporates -> amorphous silica (opal-A) supersaturates and precipitates, often templated on microbial filaments -> beaded, spiky, terraced sinter that later recrystallises toward chert/quartz.
landforms.timescale: ~mm/yr typical accumulation at vents; recrystallisation to chert over 10^4-10^6 yr.
colour_sources: microbial mats by temperature band (carotenoid yellow/orange, cyanobacterial green, brown)

control_response.recipe: Si+O strongly toward: the most direct 'silicon builds stone' landform on Earth. [sci]
control_response.sea: Water toward. [INFERRED] Ammonia (alkaline) holds more silica in solution, so ammonia worlds would deposit sinter where fluids cool or neutralise.
control_response.heat: Hot source + cooler surface toward (needs a gradient).

landforms.name: Tufa tower
landforms.mechanism: Calcium-rich spring water rises through the floor of an alkaline, carbonate-rich lake -> where the two waters mix, CaCO3 precipitates around the vent (cool water can also form ikaite) -> chimney grows upward toward the surface -> lake level drops and leaves the towers standing on dry shore.
landforms.timescale: Towers grow over decades-centuries; Mono Lake's were exposed after water diversions began in 1941.

control_response.recipe: C+O toward on Earth; [game] Si+O variant = chemical-garden-like silica chimneys.
control_response.sea: Water (alkaline lake) toward; ammonia (alkaline) is a natural [game] fit. Acid away.

landforms.name: Karst towers (fenglin) and cone karst
landforms.mechanism: Rain picks up CO2 from air and soil -> carbonic acid dissolves limestone along joints -> joints widen into closed depressions -> depressions merge, leaving cones (fengcong) -> continued lowering to a flat floor isolates steep towers (fenglin).
landforms.timescale: 10^6-10^7 yr; limestone surfaces lower by tens of mm per 1000 yr in humid tropics.

control_response.recipe: C+O toward on Earth. [game] Whatever rock the sea dissolves becomes karst.
control_response.sea: Acid strongly toward; water toward. [INFERRED] Methane dissolves organics, so methane worlds get karst in organic rock (Titan labyrinths, see notes/02).
control_response.heat: Warm-wet toward (tropical karst is most dramatic).
control_response.light: Indirect: bright = more plants = more soil CO2.
control_response.hunger: Indirect: more life = more CO2 = faster dissolution.

landforms.name: Cave formations (speleothems)
landforms.mechanism: Water saturated with Ca-bicarbonate drips into an air-filled cave with lower CO2 -> degasses -> calcite precipitates: stalactites (down), stalagmites (up), columns where they meet, flowstone, rimstone dams.
landforms.timescale: Typically ~0.01-1 mm/yr; metre-scale stalagmites in 10^3-10^5 yr.

control_response.recipe: C+O toward on Earth; [game] Si+O variant = opal drips.
control_response.sea: Water toward. Acid: dissolves more than it deposits (sulfuric-acid caves like Carlsbad grow gypsum).
control_response.light: Dark (it's underground) - pairs with R8 glow.

landforms.name: Columnar jointing
landforms.mechanism: Thick lava flow (or welded tuff) cools from its top and bottom -> rock contracts and cracks perpendicular to the cooling front -> cracks advance inward in steps, reorganising toward a hexagonal network (120-degree junctions) -> straight polygonal columns; faster cooling makes thinner columns.
landforms.timescale: Forms in years-decades as a flow cools; exposed by erosion over 10^4-10^7 yr.

control_response.recipe: Si+O strongly toward (silicate melts). Also forms in starch and some ices [sci], so it is a generic contraction pattern.
control_response.sea: Water toward (quenching gives thinner, more regular columns). [INFERRED]
control_response.heat: Hot (volcanic) world, then cooled; [game] Heat high + Si high = hexagon fields.
control_response.time: Young to form; mid-old to expose.

landforms.name: Dunes (barchan, transverse, linear, star)
landforms.mechanism: Wind lifts sand into saltation -> sand piles where flow slows -> dune shape set by sand supply and how many wind directions there are: barchan (crescent) = little sand, one wind; transverse = lots of sand, one wind; linear (seif) = two alternating winds; star = winds from many directions. Dunes either grow in bed-instability mode or elongate from a fixed source.
landforms.timescale: Barchans migrate metres to tens of metres per year; large linear/star dunes 10^3-10^5 yr; dune reddening by iron coatings over 10^4-10^5 yr.
colour_sources: hematite grain coatings (red, deepens with age and distance)

control_response.recipe: Si+O toward (quartz sand, R2). C-only worlds lack durable sand unless organics (Titan).
control_response.sea: Dry or methane toward (Titan has huge linear organic dunes [sci]); water oceans away locally.
control_response.time: Young-mid for shape; old for red colour.

landforms.name: Patterned ground and ice-wedge polygons
landforms.mechanism: (a) Polygons: in permafrost, winter cold shrinks the ground -> thermal-contraction cracks -> meltwater fills and freezes -> wedge grows each year -> polygon net 10-30 m across. (b) Sorted circles/stripes: repeated freeze-thaw heaves stones up and sideways; stones and fines self-sort into circles on flats and stripes on slopes.
landforms.timescale: Cracks open every winter; mature polygons and sorted circles in centuries-millennia.
colour_sources: sorted contrast: pale stones vs dark fines

control_response.recipe: Neutral (any rock).
control_response.sea: Water strongly toward on Earth; [INFERRED] any frozen/thawing volatile could do it (Mars, Pluto's convection cells in N2 ice).
control_response.heat: Cold with seasonal crossings toward; hot away.

landforms.name: Desert (rock) varnish
landforms.mechanism: Wind-blown dust and dew settle on stable rock faces -> clay plus manganese and iron oxides build a thin coat (<200 micrometres) -> Mn is enriched ~50-100x over crust; leading recent hypothesis: cyanobacteria accumulate Mn as an antioxidant and leave it behind -> black or brown sheen, streaked where water runs.
landforms.timescale: Very slow: ~1-40 micrometres per 1000 years.

examples.name: Varnished cliffs
examples.place: Valley of Fire State Park, Nevada, USA

control_response.recipe: O toward (oxides). [game] dark-stained arches (eco-15) fit.
control_response.sea: Dry/arid toward; humid washes it off.
control_response.light: Bright toward if microbial: UV stress drives Mn uptake. [PEER, disputed]
control_response.time: Strong: varnish darkness is a natural age readout (R3).

landforms.name: Coloured strata (Danxia, rainbow mountains)
landforms.mechanism: Sands and muds pile up in basins under changing climates -> each layer gets a different iron state and mineral mix (oxidising arid conditions -> red hematite; wetter/reducing -> green, grey, yellow) -> mountain-building tilts and folds the stack -> erosion exposes stripes; Danxia red-bed cliffs are cut into towers and walls.
landforms.timescale: Deposition over 10^6-10^7 yr (Cretaceous red beds at Zhangye); exposure over the last few million years.

control_response.recipe: O strongly toward red; low O toward green/grey. [sci] analogue.
control_response.sea: R3 mapping: water -> iron red; acid -> sulfur yellow; methane -> tholin orange; ammonia -> plum [game].
control_response.time: Strong: stripes are layered history; [game] each Time era could lay a band in the current sea's stain colour.

landforms.name: Salt flat / evaporite crust (incl. sulfur fields)
landforms.mechanism: Closed basin collects brine -> sun and wind evaporate it -> halite (and gypsum) crystallise into a crust -> flood-evaporate cycles stack layers -> below the crust, salty groundwater convects in cells; salt precipitates over the downwelling edges, raising a polygon net of ridges ~1-2 m across. At Dallol, hot acid brines plus volcanic sulfur and iron give yellow-green-orange crusts.
landforms.timescale: Polygon ridges re-form in weeks-months after flooding; salt pans accumulate over 10^4 yr.
colour_sources: iron chlorides/oxides (green -> orange as they oxidise)

control_response.recipe: Neutral for halite; O+S for sulfate/sulfur crusts.
control_response.sea: Water (evaporating) toward; acid toward sulfur-yellow crusts (R3) [sci analogue: Dallol]. Methane: Titan lake-bed evaporites are proposed [PEER, see notes/02].

landforms.name: Mushroom / pedestal rock
landforms.mechanism: Two routes. (a) Wind: saltating sand stays within ~1-2 m of the ground, so abrasion is strongest low down and undercuts a stem. (b) Moisture/hardness: the base stays damp longer and weathers faster, or a hard cap (concretion, harder bed) shields soft rock below. Most real pedestals combine both.

examples.name: Mushroom Rock (1916 photo)
examples.place: Mushroom Rock State Park, Kansas, USA

control_response.recipe: Si+O sand needed for the wind route (R2 sand).
control_response.sea: Dry toward; methane (Titan winds + sand) plausibly toward [INFERRED].
control_response.hunger: Neutral. [game] Shape echoes R7 parasols, so abiotic 'parasol rocks' could be a visual pun on dead worlds.

landforms.status: disputed (relative role of wind vs basal weathering)
